text: Process Canvas ports (emits, dataFlow, channels, parentMemberId, stage) are declarative-only: the agent still applies the label at runtime, and graph edges are derived from these ports — so dropping a port entry corrupts the model/graph without necessarily changing runtime routing.

Recovering interrupted prior-run work: a crashed/interrupted run may leave an issue's WIP in a git STASH (not only in the working tree or a bare branch) — run 'git stash list' before assuming work was reverted/lost. Note 'git checkout stash@{N} -- <files>' STAGES those files, so a later gh-as-agent commit of other work sweeps them in; unstash into a scratch area or reset the index if you need separate commits.

Lucide role-template icons live in shared admin-console/src/components/role-icons.js (ROLE_ICONS map + roleIcon(name) helper, default User); TeamSetup.jsx and ProcessCanvas.jsx AddRoleDialog both import it — don't re-duplicate the map (created in PR #593 for #586 AC1).
GitHub issues/tickets in 314092_agent-execution-environment are always authored in English, even when the requesting human chats in another language (e.g. German).

To integration-test a commit-making CLI's git behaviour (knowledge/gh-as-agent) without an ambient identity, run the real CLI as a subprocess inside a temp `git init` repo with a stripped identity: HOME=empty tmp dir, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM=os.devnull, and GIT_AUTHOR/COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL popped from env.

When a CLI tool wraps a git commit, extract identity args into a pure `build_commit_args()`-style helper so unit tests can assert the inline `-c user.name/user.email` flags without running git; the integration test then runs the full CLI against a stripped-identity env to close the gap.

buildAgentClaudeMd has TWO call sites whose output must stay byte-identical — saveAgentPrompt (seed) and the /internal/agents/:id/prompt-preview endpoint; any new per-agent opt (skills, skillDescriptions, knowledgeDigestRef) MUST be threaded through both or the preview diverges from what's seeded.

When a prompt-assembly.js enrichment reads data from disk, the I/O helper belongs in orchestrator.js (fail-soft, try/catch per item) while the pure renderer in prompt-assembly.js stays fs-free and accepts the data as a caller-supplied map — see agentSkillDescriptions + skillsSection pattern in PR #618.

For AC6 (preview == seed) in CLAUDE.md composition features: both `saveAgentPrompt` and the `/internal/agents/:id/prompt-preview` endpoint must be updated to pass the same enrichment data to buildAgentClaudeMd — verify both call sites in every prompt-assembly PR.

When a dialog has single vs multi-item phrasing, use a derived boolean flag (e.g. `single = aggregated && count <= 1`) to branch copy only — leave controls, submit logic, and checkbox behaviour untouched; the flag is purely presentational.

When threading graph-node data from a section component into a dialog (e.g. teamSkills for extend-target picker), pass it as a second argument to the callback prop (onReviewSuggestion(s, skills)) and store it on the state object that opens the dialog — single source of truth, no separate fetch needed.

The skill.json startup backfill (and any bulk write to the GLOBAL skill pool) MUST live in admin-console, not the orchestrator: the orchestrator mounts /template-workspace (=/pool/skills) READ-ONLY, while admin-console mounts /pool RW. Both mount /workspace (team+agent skills) RW. So orchestrator can only stamp team-tier skills (_teamSkillDir) and agent dirs.

Two-sided module pattern (skill-manifest, knowledge-digest): when reviewing, run 'node --test' on BOTH test suites and verify byte-identical guard (test case that diffs the two files) passes — this is the only automated drift detector between admin-console and orchestrator copies.

skill-manifest.js copy semantics: stampSkillCopy (promote/lift/share) discards the cpSync-dragged skill.json before re-stamping (fresh v1 chain + origin); stampSkill (import, edit, create) reads any existing manifest and continues the chain — concept §3.1 / §3.5. Verify correct choice when reviewing any new copy-creating path.

Adding an optional field to the two-sided knowledge store (orchestrator/knowledge-store.js + agent-image/scripts/knowledge) stays JSONL byte-identical iff appended LAST in KEY_ORDER on BOTH mirrors and only emitted when a non-empty trimmed string; an absent field then serializes exactly as before, so the digest (reads text only) is provably unchanged. Assert with a 'field absent unless supplied round-trips identical' test on both the JS (node --test) and Python (test_knowledge.py) suites.

Route-level display overlay pattern in admin-console/api/api.js: compute read-time-only display fields (e.g. augmentDisplaySummary, sibling of augmentDigestInclusion) in the /api/knowledge/graph route AFTER the pure graph builder, so the pure builder stays entries+skills-only and never depends on LLM/heuristic display logic. Persist only authoritative values (real LLM summaries) via the canonical overlay in runConvergenceCollector/_serializeCanonicalKind, carried forward across convergence only while the entry text is unchanged (text edit -> regenerate).

When a new optional field is added to a two-sided JS+Python KB store, the KEY_ORDER, makeKnowledgeEntry/build_entry, and validateKnowledgeEntry must all be updated in BOTH mirrors and both cross-runtime GOLDEN tests must pass — no summary field emitted when absent means serialisation is byte-identical to pre-PR output.

Carry-forward pattern for re-projection-derived fields (summary, #635): read prior canonical files before re-projecting, carry each entry's field forward only when prev.text === e.text, so a text change drops the stale field and triggers regeneration on the next write pass.

Skill move-transfer strand guard (skill-transfer #626): a move to GLOBAL never strands (universal fallback remains); a move to a TEAM tier can orphan grantees OUTSIDE that team -> POST /api/skills/transfer returns 409 with the agent-id list unless force:true (or a global copy of the name still exists). Move always archives the source to /workspace/skill-archive/<tierSeg>/<name>-<hash>-<ts>/ before deleting.

When a PR adds a new UI action that supersedes an existing button, the old button must be removed in the same PR — leaving both co-existing fails the 'no-provenance paths gone from UI' criterion and creates a confusing dual-action UI (seen in PR #638 team→global: two buttons, one without provenance).

When a PR introduces an engine that supersedes old endpoints, the Code Reviewer treats ANY surviving old UI call to the deprecated endpoint as an AC violation (esp. no-provenance paths) — grep the .jsx for the deprecated endpoint URLs, remove the button AND its wrapper fn, not just the backend.

CodeQL 'uncontrolled data used in path expression' on admin-console skill endpoints clears by routing the filesystem probe through the containment-guarded resolver (transferSkillExistsAt / resolveTransferSkillDir, which use path.resolve+path.relative) — a raw path.join on an already-SKILL_NAME_RE-validated name still trips the query; do NOT add redundant validation.

Reworker: on every wake compare the SHA the latest review examined (review body / git show -s --format=%ci) against current branch HEAD before re-doing work — a fix that lands seconds before the revisions-required label still counts; if HEAD already resolves the findings, re-verify (grep deprecated symbols + run tests) and re-hand-back with a PR comment flagging the timing race instead of re-editing.

When reviewing a skill-tier engine PR (#626 pattern), always check KnowledgeFlow.jsx fetch() calls — the ShareDialog and lift path use /api/knowledge/share-to-team and /api/knowledge/promote which are separate from /api/skills/transfer; the issue key-files list is the reliable guide to which files must be changed.

Reworker: when a Code Reviewer promotes a previously-declared-NON-blocking item to a blocker across review passes AND the requested fix would regress functionality, escalate with a blocking PR comment quoting the earlier pass rather than silently complying; fix any clean sibling items but do NOT re-apply ready-for-review while the contested blocker is open.

Reworker: when escalating a PR to a human (contradictory/impossible/product-decision review feedback), apply the 'human-decision-required' label (magenta #5319E7, created in 314092 repo 2026-07-16) to the PR in addition to the blocking comment — do NOT re-apply ready-for-review while it is set, and remove it once the question is resolved and the PR is handed back. Label makes the paused-for-human state visible in the PR list.

In process-template bundles, the CI lint guard (process-template-registry.test.js 'render with no error/warning lints') builds the graph ONLY from roles' emits/github/channels/triggers — NOT from the labels[] registry; adding/removing a labels entry is lint-safe as long as the bundle still passes validateProcessTemplate (which only checks labels is an array). The gate-violation lint fires only on an agent's emits of a human:*-PREFIXED label.

Label-schema convention for a 'pause-for-human' signal that an AGENT applies (e.g. human-decision-required in core-sdlc.json): { humanGate: false, brake: true } — brake=pauses the loop (like hold/needs:human), humanGate:false because the agent (not a human) sets it.

core-sdlc.json label schema: humanGate=true means a human applies the label (e.g. 'ready'); humanGate=false means an agent applies it; brake=true means the label pauses the automated loop pending a human decision (e.g. 'human-decision-required'); brake=false means it is a routing signal only.

Skill deletion (skill-deletion.js #627): DELETE /api/skills/:name guards all tiers uniformly (409 lists blocking constructs), cascade:true deactivates blocking grants then deletes; the snapshot MUST be taken BEFORE cascade (an agent-tier cascade removes the very dir) and rolled back on a refused 409 delete so a blocked attempt leaves no orphan archive. Team Admin can delete a team skill without System Admin (permitDeletion team tier).

Skill archive layout (#627): every delete snapshots to /workspace/skill-archive/<tierSeg>/<name>-<hash>-<ts>/ + an archive-meta.json sidecar (same dir layout skill-transfer's MOVE writes — moved+deleted skills share ONE restore surface; deliberately a directory, NOT the ZIP the concept §3.3 wording implies). Restore via POST /api/skills/archive/restore excludes archive-meta.json from the restored dir; prune via planArchivePrune (pure, default 90d, System-Admin only).

When an issue lists KnowledgeFlow.jsx as a key file alongside a permission-gating AC for Team Admins, verify BOTH the backend gate AND the frontend route guard — AdminRoute (user.admin = sysadmin/envAdmin only) blocks Team Admins from SkillsRegistry; the fix belongs in either the route or KnowledgeFlow.jsx.

Cold-nav-safe deep-link into agent chat: navigate to /chats/<agentId>?session=<correlationId> (a bookmarkable query param, not router state); AgentChat.jsx consumes it via useSearchParams only after the agent list has loaded + agent exists (consumedSessionRef guards re-fire), then strips the param with setSearchParams(replace:true). Reuse the existing railTabRequest {tab,ts} mechanism (thread a sibling sessionSelectRequest {correlationId,ts} down AgentChat->RightRail(selectRequest)->SessionsPanel) rather than inventing a parallel one (PR #645, issue #642 AC4/AC7).

Deep-link via query param pattern (e.g. ?session=<correlationId>): consume in AgentChat.jsx once agents load with a consumedRef guard; propagate via a *Request state (with ts: Date.now() for re-trigger); the receiving panel does its own fresh API fetch with a cancel flag so stale async results never update state after unmount.

Reworker/#627: the Team-Admin-accessible skill-delete UI belongs on the Knowledge page (KnowledgeFlow.jsx) team SkillCard, NOT the System-Admin Skills Registry (which is behind <AdminRoute> and mixes global-pool ops). Add a Trash2 action gated on skill.tier==='team' calling DELETE /api/skills/:name?source=team&teamId=&cascade=true, mirroring the Registry's 409-guard + one-click cascade; backend permitDeletion/canManageTeam stays the security boundary (no client-side role gate, matching the page's existing activate/deactivate actions).

admin-console AC that requires a Team-Admin UI capability: check whether the target page is behind <AdminRoute> in App.jsx (user.admin = sysadmin/envAdmin only). If so, the capability must live on a non-adminOnly page such as /knowledge (KnowledgeFlow.jsx) rather than opening the System-Admin page (Skills Registry/etc.) to Team Admins, since those pages expose global-scope ops that would 403 and break the #584 AC8 System-Admin-only-page design.

Skill deletion archive (skill-deletion.js #627): DELETE takes a snapshot BEFORE the guard check; snapshot is rolled back on 409 so a refused cascade never leaves an orphan archive — the ordering is intentional and must be preserved in future delete-path changes.

skill-manifest.js forceHistory (added #628): an additive default-off stampManifest option that records a history entry + refreshes updatedAt/updatedBy WITHOUT bumping the version when contentHash is unchanged — used by the import round-trip so an export→import of byte-identical content continues the version chain and appends an 'imported' event (concept never-reset), instead of an endpoint-side history hack. Must be mirrored into BOTH byte-identical copies + a fixture stampCase.

skill-import.js anti-drift guard: skill-import.test.js asserts parseFrontmatterField(c, 'description') === parseSkillDescription(c) across 6 canonical cases — run this test when touching either parser to catch cross-module drift (issue #628, PR #646).

forceHistory:true on stampSkill/stampSkillDir appends a history entry and refreshes updatedAt/updatedBy without bumping version — the correct stamp for a provenance-only lifecycle event (import round-trip) where content is byte-identical; additive and default-off, mirrored into both byte-identical skill-manifest.js copies (PR #646).

Skill drift is computed on READ from three hashes (copy current, seed-time anchor in .aee/seeded-skills.json.contentHash, source current) via classifyCopyDrift in the byte-mirrored skill-manifest.js; a deleted source MUST be detected by absent SKILL.md, not by hashing the empty dir. Only 'outdated' is resyncable; resync reuses the additive _syncSkillIntoWorkspace path (no respawn) and is idempotent; diverged/conflict/orphaned/unknown are refused. Auto-resync gate skillResyncMode (default review) fans out only to 'auto' teams on a source edit (#629).

When a skill-drift feature overlays drift state on the API list and knowledge graph, all three edit paths (PUT /api/skills/:name team branch, global branch, and PUT /api/skills/:name/file) must call autoResyncOnEdit — missing one leaves a silent gap in the auto-resync fan-out.

Drift is a property of copies (seeded agent workspace replicas, team copies of a global skill), not sources — drift badges belong on the Knowledge graph surface (KnowledgeFlow.jsx SkillCard) where member copies are visible, not on the Skills Registry where source pool skills are managed.

POST /api/skills/install (admin-console/api/api.js) delegates to the orchestrator /internal/agents/:id/skills/activate path — it writes the grant + syncs files with team-first resolution like a re-seed; it no longer does an ad-hoc cpSync file copy. The grant edit is the pure planAgentGrantEdit in orchestrator/skill-grants.js; a team-member's per-agent install writes skillsOverride materializing the inherited grant (fixes #630 AC1: install can no longer diverge from a full re-seed).

In this sandbox admin-console/ and orchestrator/ have no node_modules, so .jsx has no unit-test harness and auth.test.js fails on a missing express-rate-limit require (pre-existing/environmental, passes in CI). Validate JSX syntax with 'npx esbuild --loader=jsx' reading the file on stdin (exit 0 = clean parse); do NOT pass --bundle=false (invalid for transform).

When an install/copy endpoint is replaced by a delegation to the orchestrator's activate path, remove the admin-console containment check for the source dir (now handled by the orchestrator's resolveSkillSourceDir) but keep the containment check for the destination dir — CodeQL tracks the inflow in api.js, not the delegated path.

planAgentGrantEdit (#630): team-member must materialise the full effective (inherited) grant into skillsOverride before appending — failing to do so silently drops all inherited team skills from the member's grant. The test case 'materializing the inherited grant' is the key regression guard.

For operator-triggered destructive git actions in the admin-console proxy, the AC7 running-session re-check belongs at the proxy layer (reads running-sessions.json directly before forwarding) — not duplicated in the orchestrator endpoint, since the proxy is the single control-plane gate before git commands run (#648 pattern).

When a Workspace Git panel endpoint enriches GET /api/agents/:id/workspace/git-status with branch metadata (currentBranch, branches[], detached, hasRemote, hasUpstream, dirty), derive those fields from a pure read-only helper (readRepoBranchMeta) that runs only local git commands and spreads into the existing response shape — keeps the status endpoint non-breaking and avoids a separate endpoint (#648).

Skill merge (#631, skill-merge.js): merge folds N skills into one target; provenance UNIONs sources' entryIds, extra-file collisions namespace under files/<source>/, grants naming a retired source migrate to the target (activate target FIRST then deactivate sources via orchestrator /internal/{teams,agents}/:id/skills/{activate,deactivate}), retired sources archived via the uniform archiveDeletedSkill path; retireSources defaults ON; target-tier permission (same permit helper as transfer/deletion). Pure planner + api.js IO caller, mirrors skill-transfer/skill-deletion.

admin-console/api tests: node_modules is often NOT installed in the agent environment, so 'node --test' fails auth.test.js with 'Cannot find module express-rate-limit' (api.js/auth.js require it). This is environmental, not a regression — verify feature work by running the pure test files directly (e.g. node --test skill-merge.test.js) + node --check api.js + esbuild parse of the .jsx, and note the unrelated auth failure in the PR.

Skill merge (#631) pure-planner pattern: skill-merge.js is fs-free (pure validator + planner), api.js does all IO — same 'pure core + IO caller' discipline as skill-transfer.js / skill-deletion.js; the stampSkillCopy (fresh v1 chain) is correct for a merge because the merged skill is a new entity.

In POST /api/skills/merge grant migration, the target skill must be activated FIRST via the orchestrator (before deactivating each source) so no member workspace is left without the skill during the transition window.

Token usage telemetry (#654): the canonical usage-record schema is a two-sided golden-fixture contract — admin-console/api/usage-summary.fixture.json is asserted by BOTH the JS aggregator (usage-summary.test.js) and the Python emitter build_usage_record (test_agent_entrypoint.py); change both sides in one commit. Records are day-bucketed JSONL at /workspace/usage/usage-<date>.jsonl (single-writer orchestrator, NO retention). total_cost_usd is stored opaque and NEVER surfaced (tokens only).

Token telemetry run_context must be built on ALL call paths (cron, github-event, http, DM) — the DM path in phase 1 omits it, leaving trigger/github null on DM records; flag as a follow-up when reviewing phase 2 token attribution.

For new telemetry endpoints, verify the golden fixture covers the null/None case for every optional field (trigger, github, modelUsage) — the aggregator's handling of null values should be tested explicitly alongside the structured-value cases.

Validating admin-console JSX with esbuild (no node_modules): 'npx esbuild --loader=jsx <path>' FAILS ('loader without extension only applies to stdin') when given a FILE PATH — use 'npx esbuild --loader:.jsx=jsx <path>' for paths, or pipe the file via stdin ('npx esbuild --loader=jsx < file').

When reviewing a PR branch that accumulated multiple preceding merged sub-PRs, diff against the last merged PR's merge-base commit (git diff <last-merge-sha>...HEAD) rather than origin/main to isolate only the new work — the three-dot diff is the right tool.

Lazy lineage fetch pattern in SkillViewer (#632): reset lineage to null on skill change (skillKey effect), fetch only when tab !== 'content' and lineage is null — a single round-trip gate so file browsing stays fast.

Token telemetry (#655): usage records carry TWO repo identities — github.repo is owner/name (stamped by the poller) while git.repo is the short clone-dir basename; pr-events records must normalize to owner/name (repoFullName from PR/remote URL) so artifact-graph keys match tier-B nodes, and tier-C branch joins reconcile the short git.repo against the owner/name tail.

For work-item attribution PRs: verify the pr-events graph-building pass reads ALL pr-events records WITHOUT a `since` window filter — a PR opened before the query window still owns runs inside it; only the usage-run pass is windowed by since/until.

Tier-C (branch) attribution proxy for agent authorship: require `rec.git.headAfter !== rec.git.headBefore` (HEAD moved = agent committed); no @agents.local author-field check needed because only agent runs emit usage records.

Skill-grant validation (skill-grant-validate.js #633): validateGrantNames(submitted, known, previous) rejects a name only if it is NEITHER a known skill NOR already in the prior grant — this resolves the AC2-vs-AC4 tension (block newly-typed unknowns, but preserve pre-existing dead grants so they're flagged in the UI, not dropped). Wired into PUT /api/agents/:id (skills for non-members, skillsOverride for members) + POST /api/teams(/stream) (create-mode uses previous=[] and global-only known set since the team pool doesn't exist yet). SkillPicker.jsx v2 takes skill OBJECTS (skills prop, not allSkills names) from GET /api/skills.

When a phased-feature branch (phase N) is built on top of an unmerged phase-(N-1) branch, git diff origin/main...HEAD spans both phases; use git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD to enumerate each commit and git show <sha> --stat to isolate the new work from the prerequisite foundation before writing the AC verdict.

When reviewing a grant-validation PR, check POST /api/agents/:teamId/members as a gap — it accepts skillsOverride but bypasses any /api/agents/:id validation. It is typically out of issue scope (not in key files) but worth a non-blocking note.

SkillPicker v2 prop interface (PR #662): `skills` (array of skill objects, not names), `selected` (array of names), `onChange`, optional `emptyHint`. buildRows collapses to one row per name (team-first) and appends unknown selected names as flagged rows.

Skill file-write refactor (#639): one shared IO core commitSkillWrite() in admin-console/api/api.js does the dir materialise+SKILL.md/provenance write+skill.json stamp for ALL landing paths (transfer, promote/lift, share, extend); collision decision is the pure skill-transfer.planSkillWrite({onCollision,exists,allowExisting}). stamp.mode 'copy'=stampSkillCopy (fresh v1 chain), 'chain'=stampSkill (continue). share-to-team now copies the FULL dir (copyFrom) with provenance written AFTER as an override. When reviewing new copy-creating skill paths, verify they route through commitSkillWrite, not raw cpSync.

When reviewing a shared-core extraction PR (e.g. commitSkillWrite #639), enumerate all callers and verify each passes the correct stamp.mode — 'chain' for in-place extend (continues existing chain), 'copy' for all new-instance paths (fresh v1 chain, discards dragged manifest). A wrong mode silently breaks skill lineage.

orchestrator/ and admin-console/api/ have NO package-lock.json, so CI uses `npm install` there (npm ci hard-fails without a lockfile); only admin-console/ has a lockfile and uses `npm ci --include=dev`.
For CI-only PRs, the meaningful diff is just the new workflow file — use 'git show <top-commit-sha>' to isolate scope, as the branch may include many already-merged commits if it was cut behind main.

A unit test for behaviour gated on a baked absolute path (e.g. PATH-prepend keyed off FAKE_CLAUDE_DIR=/opt/ace/e2e) is vacuous unless it injects a real temp dir via patch.object + writes the sentinel file — otherwise the exists() branch is never true in a repo checkout and the test passes without exercising the code.

When a new Node package (e.g. e2e/) installs via `npm ci` in the Makefile/CI, verify `package-lock.json` is committed — its absence is the most common silent break for a new harness (seen in PR #675).

For E2E-phase PRs whose runtime-dependent ACs cannot be verified from the sandbox (no podman/browser), the reviewer still blocks on the concrete code-level prerequisite (missing lockfile) and requires a `workflow_dispatch` green run before approving.

First-run Setup Wizard (SetupWizard.jsx, #671) is 3 infra steps: Model Provider (required) + SSH Key + GitHub Token (optional); the Working Environment and First Agent steps were dropped and first-run no longer creates a standalone agent. GET /api/setup/status returns exactly those 3 steps (pure builder buildSetupStatus in admin-console/api/setup-status.js), isComplete driven solely by the required Model Provider step, and finish/skip routes to /team-setup.

Reworker: a Playwright e2e package's package-lock.json must be committed for `make e2e`/`npm ci` to work — generate it with `npm install --package-lock-only` (lockfileVersion 3 + integrity, no node_modules download) and verify via `npm ci --dry-run`; it is NOT gitignored (only /e2e/node_modules/, test-results/, playwright-report/, .auth/ are).

Reworker: when the only Blocking review item is fixable and the remaining ACs are reviewer-marked 'Pending' and structurally gated on a real CI runner (already noted by the PR author), resolve the blocker and hand back ready-for-review with a PR comment explaining the runner-gated items — do NOT escalate/human-decision-required, since a known CI limitation is not a contradiction or product decision.

When a wizard step and a settings page share the same auth UI (e.g. OAuthLoginWizard), extract it to src/components/ as a shared component imported by both — this is the implementation pattern for an AC8-style 'two surfaces must not drift' requirement.

For wizard steps that use shared payload logic (build + gate), extract both helpers to a sibling .js file (e.g. setup-wizard-payload.js) free of React/DOM so they can be tested with node --test — the wizard save-gate and the payload builder must be driven by the same function to prevent drift.

For E2E harness PRs where some ACs require infra unavailable in the agent sandbox (podman runner, browser), the correct review posture is: confirm all unit-testable ACs locally, verify CI job structure is correct, apply ready-to-merge, and let the first nightly run close the runner-gated ACs — do not block on infrastructure ACs when the implementation and fallbacks are sound.

When a shared ConnectionsSection-style component gains a new rendering mode (dropdown vs text-input) controlled by a new prop (stages=[]), always check all consumers for a showStage=false guard — that is the no-regression path for shared UI sections that multiple node-inspector hosts use.

For orchestrator-side GitHub comment posting (not agent-session), inlining <!-- agent: <id> --> is functionally equivalent to gh-as-agent stamp — the key loop-protection check is whether the action event type (IssueCommentEvent) can re-fire the triggering callback; PR-merge detection fires only on PullRequestEvent closed+merged, so a comment post carries no self-trigger risk (#678 pattern).

admin-console React fetch effects must never list a state they set (e.g. a *Loading flag) in their dependency array — it tears the effect down mid-flight and the cleanup's cancelled-guard suppresses the setState calls, hanging the UI (SkillViewer lineage tabs bug #681/#659); guard on the resolved states (data || error) instead.

For volume-isolation CLI tools that mirror `knowledge` (phase-N in telemetry concept): verify (1) agent_id is path-quoted with urllib.parse.quote(safe='') to prevent path traversal, (2) no-money guarantee is tested by injecting cost fields into records and grepping serialised output, (3) readRecords regex-filters filenames before path.join, (4) teamId resolution is fail-closed at the orchestrator (unknown agent → null → empty, never all-teams).

When a PR adds a read-side companion to an existing write-side module (e.g. usage-log.js adding listDayFiles/readRecords), verify the read functions are best-effort (return [] on any error) to match the write side's 'never throws' contract — consistent with the day-bucketed JSONL pattern.

React useEffect self-cancellation pattern: when a loading-state flag is both set inside an effect AND listed in its dependency array, React tears the effect down mid-flight (cleanup cancels the fetch) and re-runs it on every state change — guard on resolved terminal states (data || error) instead of the in-progress flag, and keep the in-progress flag out of the dependency array entirely.

Workspace file viewer inline media: the /api/agents/:id/workspace/file endpoint sniffs type but caps reads at 512 KB (returns {binary:true,content:null}); to serve image/media bytes add a SEPARATE streaming endpoint (e.g. /workspace/image) that fs.createReadStream's the full file with the real Content-Type under the same safeAgentPath guard, and signal the type to the UI via an added field on /file — do not widen /file's cap.

Detect image format by magic bytes not extension (PNG 89504E47 0D0A1A0A, JPEG FFD8FF, GIF 'GIF8[79]a', WebP 'RIFF'....'WEBP') in a pure admin-console/api/*.js CJS module for node --test coverage; SVG has no raster magic so it naturally falls back to the binary placeholder (also avoids the inline-SVG XSS surface).

For inline binary-streaming workspace endpoints (/workspace/image pattern): auth is covered by the global `app.use('/api', auth.gate)` middleware — no per-route auth needed; always set X-Content-Type-Options:nosniff and detect content by magic bytes (not extension) when serving user-controlled file bytes.

The 'Draft with AI' skill combine flow uses ONE pure builder buildSkillDraftRequest(candidate) in admin-console/api/knowledge-suggestions.js feeding BOTH endpoints (POST /api/knowledge/draft and POST /api/knowledge/promotion-suggestions/:id/draft); buildHeuristicSkillDraft is the no-LLM fallback. max_tokens is returned by the builder and spread into the api.js payload, so scaling the token/word budget lives entirely in the pure module — no api.js change needed.

For LLM prompt-scaling PRs (budget tiers, max_tokens), verify both ends: the large-combine truncation fix (max_tokens floor for 100+ items) and the small-combine padding guard (AC to prevent over-structuring 2–3 items) must each have dedicated tests.

React inline styles: a `padding` (or any) shorthand placed AFTER its longhand sibling in the SAME style object silently overrides the longhand (e.g. `padding:'3px 8px'` after `paddingLeft: X` resets paddingLeft to 8px) — use longhand-only when a computed paddingLeft/Top/etc must survive.

For WorkspaceBrowser visual indent fixes, the key invariant is: file Row gutter must mirror DirNode's Caret gutter (11px + 2px gap = 13px) so both land at paddingLeft + 13 at the same depth; DirContents passes depth=parentDepth+1 to both Row and child DirNode, so depth arithmetic is always consistent.

When a React inline-style object sets a CSS shorthand (e.g. padding:'3px 8px') AFTER a longhand (paddingLeft:...) in the same object literal, the shorthand wins and silently discards the longhand — the fix is always to replace the shorthand with its constituent longhands.

Per-room session logs (sessions/<roomId>.jsonl) now rotate by size into <roomId>.<seq>.jsonl archives (#673): a rotation policy is mirrored two-sided (orchestrator/session-rotation.js <-> _archive_name/_parse_archive_seq/_plan_prune in agent-entrypoint.py) and admin-console/api/session-archives.js resolves an archive filename back to its base room; SSE byte-cursor tailing stays live-file-only while history/correlationId-backfill span archives+live. Don't assume one growing session file.

For session-log rotation PRs: verify (1) drain-before-live-file ordering in the push thread, (2) rotate command idempotency via archive existence check, (3) both sides prune after rotation, and (4) the size < cursor path triggers SSE _truncated re-backfill — these are the four gate checks.
